edits.old: Spoken guidance can help mixed-reality users locate objects outside their current field of view. Voice identity may also affect how users experience that assistance. Follow My Voice compares a participant-preferred catalog voice with a synthetic version of the participant's own voice. Target identity is withheld while gaze-contingent directions guide search across eight surrounding vertical planes. A right-controller ray and trigger provide explicit selection.
edits.new: Spoken guidance can help mixed-reality users locate objects outside their current field of view, and the identity of the guiding voice may also shape how that assistance is experienced. Follow My Voice compares a participant-preferred catalog voice with a synthetic version of the participant's own voice. Target identity is withheld; instead, gaze-contingent spoken directions guide search across eight surrounding vertical planes, while a right-controller ray and trigger provide explicit selection.
edits.reason: Joins the choppy opening declaratives into a motivated sequence. Content is unchanged.

edits.old: The system separates local spatial reasoning from constrained language-model decisions. A central guidance state machine combines valid gaze, controller intersections, and recent history. Jev selects eligible phrasing and speaking opportunities; local playback checks reject stale cues. Prepared ElevenLabs audio supplies both conditions. Synchronized records distinguish gaze contact, spoken acknowledgment, controller pointing, and successful selection.
edits.new: The system separates local spatial reasoning from constrained language-model decisions. A central guidance state machine combines valid gaze, controller intersections, and recent history; within those bounds, Jev selects among eligible phrasings and speaking opportunities, and local playback checks reject cues that have become stale. Prepared ElevenLabs audio supplies both conditions, and synchronized records distinguish gaze contact, spoken acknowledgment, controller pointing, and successful selection.
edits.reason: Shows how local state constrains Jev's choices. Keeps the four recorded event types distinct.

edits.old: The proposed within-participant study comprises one practice trial in the first assigned voice and two counterbalanced blocks of 40 measured trials. Analysis will compare active completion time while accounting for starting geometry and participant clustering. Workload, motivation, and agent experience will be assessed retrospectively after both blocks. This first pass documents the system, measurement definitions, planned analyses, and remaining validation requirements. Confirmatory participant outcomes are not yet available. The contribution at this stage is an auditable experimental platform and a design for studying personalized voice within a shared guidance mechanism.
edits.new: The proposed within-participant study comprises one practice trial in the first assigned voice followed by two counterbalanced blocks of 40 measured trials. The primary analysis will compare active completion time between voices while accounting for starting geometry and participant clustering. Workload, motivation, and agent experience will be rated for each block in a retrospective questionnaire administered after both blocks. This first pass documents the system, measurement definitions, planned analyses, and remaining validation requirements; confirmatory participant outcomes are not yet available. The contribution at this stage is therefore an auditable experimental platform and a design for studying personalized voice within a shared guidance mechanism.
edits.reason: Makes clear that the final-only questionnaire is referenced to each block. Ties the pending-results statement to the contribution claim.

edits.old: Gaze measurements also require careful interpretation. A ray intersecting an object is an observation made by the interaction system. It does not establish that the participant fixated, recognized, or understood the object. A nearby-gaze region is a deliberate tolerance used by the interface. It may improve usability, but it is not a substitute for measuring spatial accuracy. Similarly, a headset's nominal output rate does not demonstrate that the application receives distinct gaze observations at that rate~\cite{dunn2024reporting,niehorster2026dataquality}.
edits.new: Gaze measurements also require careful interpretation. A ray intersecting an object is an observation made by the interaction system; it does not establish that the participant fixated, recognized, or understood the object. Likewise, a nearby-gaze region is a deliberate interface tolerance that may improve usability but cannot substitute for measuring spatial accuracy. Nor does a headset's nominal output rate demonstrate that the application receives distinct gaze observations at that rate~\cite{dunn2024reporting,niehorster2026dataquality}.
edits.reason: Joins each claim to its qualification as a parallel series of cautions.

edits.old: The thesis addresses these problems by separating observed evidence, guidance state, model decisions, and delivered speech. The same distinctions carry into the analysis. An instruction selected by a model is not counted as spoken until playback starts. A qualified gaze acknowledgment is not a controller acknowledgment. A controller acknowledgment is not a successful trial until the trigger selection is correct. This separation is necessary both to implement responsive guidance and to explain what the participant actually experienced.
edits.new: The thesis addresses these problems by separating observed evidence, guidance state, model decisions, and delivered speech, and it carries the same distinctions into the analysis. An instruction selected by a model is not counted as spoken until playback starts. A qualified gaze acknowledgment is distinct from a controller acknowledgment, and a controller acknowledgment does not constitute a successful trial until the trigger selection is correct. This separation is necessary both to implement responsive guidance and to explain what the participant actually experienced.
edits.reason: Joins the chain of short negations. Gaze acknowledgment, controller acknowledgment and trigger completion stay distinct.

edits.old: Secondary questions concern perceived workload and activity experience. Will the two voices differ on the six workload dimensions and their complete unweighted mean? Will they differ on interest/enjoyment, effort/importance, pressure/tension, or value/usefulness? These outcomes concern different constructs. The analysis will preserve those distinctions rather than pool them into a broad satisfaction score.

Will they differ on interest/enjoyment, effort/importance, pressure/tension, or value/usefulness? Because these outcomes concern different constructs, the analysis will preserve those distinctions rather than pool them into a broad satisfaction score.
edits.reason: Links the rationale to the analytic decision.

edits.old: Exploratory questions concern agent perception, reliance, and the relationship between task difficulty and voice experience. Participants may describe a voice as more responsive or humanlike, may rely on guidance more often, or may experience a cloned voice as familiar or eerie. Such reports will be treated as judgments about an interaction. They will not be evidence that the system possesses intelligence, emotions, awareness, or an inner voice.

edits.old: An additional engineering objective is to make the assistance process inspectable. Can recorded state and speech history explain why a cue was eligible, why it played or was suppressed, and how long it waited? Can evaluation distinguish a genuinely unhelpful instruction from an acceptable alternative wording? These questions concern system validity and readiness. They support the empirical study but do not replace it.

edits.old: The implemented contribution is an instrumented mixed-reality guidance platform. It combines local spatial eligibility, a central guidance state machine, bounded history, constrained cloud decisions, prepared speech, and synchronized review. The resulting architecture exposes the relationship between what the system observed and what it delivered.
edits.new: The implemented contribution is an instrumented mixed-reality guidance platform that combines local spatial eligibility, a central guidance state machine, bounded history, constrained cloud decisions, prepared speech, and synchronized review. Together, these components expose the relationship between what the system observed and what it delivered.
edits.reason: Removes a stunted definition-then-list pattern.

edits.old: The project's bibliography includes several approaches to directing attention in immersive environments. Grogorick et al. address subtle gaze guidance, while HiveFive concerns immersion-preserving attention guidance~\cite{grogorick2017subtle,lange2020hivefive}. Ariza and colleagues investigate vibrotactile assistance and proximity-based multimodal feedback for selection~\cite{ariza2017vibrotactile,ariza2018proximity}. These works establish relevant design alternatives; they do not imply that all forms of guidance are equivalent. A cue that changes visual salience, a vibration that indicates proximity, and a spoken spatial instruction impose different perceptual and interpretive demands.

Ariza and colleagues investigate vibrotactile assistance and proximity-based multimodal feedback for selection~\cite{ariza2017vibrotactile,ariza2018proximity}. These works establish relevant design alternatives without implying that all forms of guidance are equivalent: a cue that changes visual salience, a vibration that indicates proximity, and a spoken spatial instruction impose different perceptual and interpretive demands.
edits.reason: Replaces the bibliography-inventory framing with a scholarly opener. Joins the qualification to its example.

edits.old: Binetti et al. examine visual and auditory cues for locating out-of-view objects in head-mounted augmented reality~\cite{binetti2021outofview}. Warden et al. focus on target cue type and location in augmented-reality search~\cite{warden2022visual}. Together, these topics make clear why target visibility and cue availability belong in the method description. Follow My Voice does not present an opening color-and-shape target description. Instead, the direction sequence gradually narrows the participant's search.
edits.new: Binetti et al. examine visual and auditory cues for locating out-of-view objects in head-mounted augmented reality~\cite{binetti2021outofview}, and Warden et al. focus on target cue type and location in augmented-reality search~\cite{warden2022visual}. Together, these studies show why target visibility and cue availability belong in the method description. Follow My Voice does not open with a color-and-shape description of the target; instead, the sequence of directions gradually narrows the participant's search.
edits.reason: Groups the related citations and smooths an awkward noun stack.

edits.old: Losing et al. connect gaze-contingent auditory feedback with visual-search guidance~\cite{losing2014guiding}. Two-Step Gaze Guidance provides another relevant precedent for staged guidance~\cite{kwok2022twostep}. The present system adopts a coarse-to-fine organization: orientation toward the correct wall precedes within-wall horizontal and vertical refinement. This is a design adaptation. Its particular geometry, phrases, timers, and confirmation regions require validation in the present apparatus.
edits.new: Losing et al. connect gaze-contingent auditory feedback with visual-search guidance~\cite{losing2014guiding}, and Two-Step Gaze Guidance provides a further precedent for staged guidance~\cite{kwok2022twostep}. The present system adapts these ideas in a coarse-to-fine organization: orientation toward the correct wall precedes within-wall horizontal and vertical refinement. Because this organization is a design adaptation, its particular geometry, phrases, timers, and confirmation regions require validation in the present apparatus.
edits.reason: Joins the stunted 'This is a design adaptation.' sentence to its consequence.

edits.old: The current study does not include an unguided or gaze-unaware control. Both voice conditions receive the same gaze-contingent policy. Earlier project documents that considered a factorial combination of voice and gaze contingency are historical, and their interpretation cannot be transferred to this two-condition design. Any observed difference will concern the assigned voice experience within the shared assistance system.
edits.new: The current study does not include an unguided or gaze-unaware control; both voice conditions receive the same gaze-contingent policy. Earlier project documents that considered a factorial combination of voice and gaze contingency are historical, and their interpretation cannot be transferred to this two-condition design. Any observed difference will therefore concern the assigned voice experience within the shared assistance system.
edits.reason: Joins related statements and makes the inference explicit.

edits.old: The experiment will use the same semantic library and provider for both conditions. That is an implementation control, not proof of equal acoustics. Prepared clips can differ in duration and pronunciation even when their text matches. Pilot checks will inspect intelligibility and comfortable playback levels across catalog and cloned voices. Actual provider, model, voice, and library identifiers will identify the configuration a participant heard.
edits.new: The experiment will use the same semantic library and provider for both conditions. This is an implementation control rather than proof of equal acoustics, because prepared clips can differ in duration and pronunciation even when their text matches. Pilot checks will therefore inspect intelligibility and comfortable playback levels across catalog and cloned voices, and the actual provider, model, voice, and library identifiers will identify the configuration each participant heard.
edits.reason: Links the control, its limitation and the planned checks causally.

edits.old: Custom experience items and the appealing, eerie, and familiar items selected from Guo et al. will remain separate. Combining them would imply a measurement model not established for this study. A participant may report a voice as both familiar and eerie. Preserving the individual directions allows that response to remain interpretable.
edits.new: Custom experience items and the appealing, eerie, and familiar items selected from Guo et al. will remain separate, since combining them would imply a measurement model not established for this study. A participant may report a voice as both familiar and eerie, and preserving the individual item directions keeps that response interpretable.
edits.reason: Joins four short declaratives into two connected sentences.

edits.old: Validation work on the Vive Pro Eye and tools such as GazeMetrics are methodological resources~\cite{schuetz2022vive,sipatchin2021usability,adhanom2020gazemetrics}. They are not substitutes for validation on the HTC Vive Focus Vision. Device model, fit, calibration, coordinate conversion, and task geometry can differ. The protocol therefore requires independent targets across heights, boundaries, distances, and head orientations. Validation targets must be separate from targets used to estimate an offset correction.

The protocol therefore requires independent targets across heights, boundaries, distances, and head orientations, and these validation targets must be separate from targets used to estimate an offset correction.

edits.old: NASA-TLX supplies six workload dimensions~\cite{hart1988nasatlx}. The project's 0--10 response range and unweighted complete mean are documented adaptations. The Intrinsic Motivation Inventory distinguishes interest/enjoyment from related subscales such as effort, pressure, and value~\cite{ryan1982control,mcauley1989imi,csdtIMI}. Separate subscale reporting preserves that distinction. The instrument appendix specifies current wording and reverse keys so scoring can be reproduced.

edits.old: Agent perception measures are drawn through Guo et al., with attribution to their originating measures~\cite{guo2024doppelganger,biocca2001networked,moussawi2019perception}. Co-presence, perceived intelligence, and anthropomorphism concern participant attributions. A high rating does not establish sentience or decision correctness. Conversely, deterministic validity checks do not establish that a participant found the agent natural. The design needs both kinds of evidence while keeping their meanings separate.

edits.old: If completion times are similar, uncertainty matters. A wide interval would leave practically important differences unresolved. A narrow interval near the null could constrain the size of a plausible effect under the tested conditions. A nonsignificant test alone will not establish equivalence. Equivalence testing is not part of the current analysis specification. Adding it would require a meaningful bound and procedure defined before inspecting the result.
edits.new: If completion times are similar, the width of the uncertainty interval becomes central. A wide interval would leave practically important differences unresolved, whereas a narrow interval near the null could constrain the size of a plausible effect under the tested conditions. A nonsignificant test alone will not establish equivalence. Equivalence testing is not part of the current analysis specification, and adding it would require a meaningful bound and procedure defined before inspecting the result.
edits.reason: Contrasts the two interval cases directly and joins fragmented sentences. The qualifications are unchanged.

edits.old: Voice condition includes more than a nominal label. The self-similar voice depends on recording quality and synthesis, while the preferred voice comes from a heterogeneous catalog. Both may differ in pitch, prosody, speaking rate, pronunciation, and clip duration. The same words and provider do not guarantee matched acoustics. The study will document these properties and pilot comfortable intelligibility rather than claim exact equivalence.
edits.new: Voice condition is more than a nominal label. The self-similar voice depends on recording quality and synthesis, whereas the preferred voice comes from a heterogeneous catalog, and the two may differ in pitch, prosody, speaking rate, pronunciation, and clip duration. Because the same words and provider do not guarantee matched acoustics, the study will document these properties and pilot comfortable intelligibility rather than claim exact equivalence.
edits.reason: Links the confound sources to the planned response.

edits.old: A shared policy does not produce identical spoken sequences. Participants turn, pause, look, and point differently. The policy consequently supplies different directions and can emit different numbers of hints. This behavior dependence is part of the design, not automatically a failure of experimental control.
edits.new: A shared policy does not produce identical spoken sequences. Because participants turn, pause, look, and point differently, the policy supplies different directions and can emit different numbers of hints. This dependence on participant behavior is part of the design, not automatically a failure of experimental control.
edits.reason: Joins cause and effect and fixes the awkward phrase 'behavior dependence'.

edits.old: One practice trial reduces setup burden but provides limited exposure to a complex interaction. A participant must learn to hold gaze on the readiness cross, follow speech, use the chair comfortably, aim the right controller, and trigger selection. The practice-proficiency rule remains to be established through pilots. A fixed single trial does not prove that every participant has acquired these skills equally.

A fixed single trial does not prove that every participant has acquired these skills equally, and the practice-proficiency rule remains to be established through pilots.
edits.reason: Reorders the sentences so the pending pilot rule follows from the stated limitation.

edits.old: Practice uses the first assigned voice. This aligns initial exposure with the first block, but also couples practice familiarity with period. Counterbalancing helps distribute this across voice conditions. It does not prevent fatigue, learning, novelty, or asymmetric carryover. These limitations will be reported with period and order effects and any relevant sensitivity analysis.
